en.title: All 5 Hunger Games Movies Return to Theaters This September
en.summary: Get ready, Panem! All five existing Hunger Games films are heading back to the big screen in a special theatrical event. This is your chance to revisit the saga before the next chapter arrives.
en.body:
The cinematic journey through Panem is set for a major revival. In an exciting announcement for fans of **Suzanne Collins**' iconic series, Fathom Entertainment and Lionsgate are bringing all five **The Hunger Games** films back to theaters nationwide. This special engagement will run from September 3 to September 7, 2026, offering a unique opportunity to experience the dystopian saga on the big screen once more.

This theatrical run serves as a grand countdown to the premiere of the highly anticipated new installment, **The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping**, which is slated for release on November 20, 2026. The screenings will feature an exclusive sneak peek of **Sunrise on the Reaping**, giving audiences their first glimpse of the next chapter in the franchise. "We're kicking off the countdown to the 50th Hunger Games by inviting audiences back to the theaters to see these epic films on the big screen," stated Kevin Grayson, President, Worldwide Distribution for the Lionsgate Motion Picture Group. "Sunrise on the Reaping is the most highly anticipated Hunger Games film yet, and to get ready, we’re proud to partner with Fathom to give audiences the opportunity to experience all five original films together in theaters."

The lineup includes the original **The Hunger Games** (2012), **The Hunger Games: Catching Fire** (2013), **The Hunger Games: Mockingjay — Part 1** (2014), **The Hunger Games: Mockingjay — Part 2** (2015), and **The Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes** (2023). The films will be screened in order of their original release dates, meaning **The Hunger Games** will play on September 3, and **The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes** will conclude the event on September 7. This chronological approach allows fans to trace the evolution of the story and its characters from the very beginning.

## A Panem Pilgrimage

For devoted fans, this event is more than just a series of movie screenings; it's a chance to reconnect with the world that has captivated millions. The **Hunger Games** franchise has a remarkable ability to spark conversation, whether it's about the intricate political machinations of the Capitol, the bravery of its protagonists, or the ethical dilemmas posed by the titular games. This theatrical return is a communal experience, bringing together a passionate global fanbase to celebrate the series' enduring legacy. It’s an opportunity to revisit iconic moments, from Katniss Everdeen's defiant act of volunteering to Coriolanus Snow's complex origins, all within the immersive environment of a cinema.

## The Road to Sunrise on the Reaping

The theatrical event is strategically timed to build maximum excitement for **The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping**. This latest film, based on **Suzanne Collins**' 2025 novel, delves into the backstory of Haymitch Abernathy, the mentor to Katniss and Peeta. Fans have expressed immense enthusiasm for exploring Haymitch's own Hunger Games experience and understanding how it shaped him. The tie-in between Lucy Gray Baird and Katniss's stories, as hinted at in **The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes**, has also generated significant buzz, with many eager to see how these narratives intertwine. The return to theaters provides the perfect prelude to uncovering these new layers of the **Hunger Games** universe.

What's Next

Mark your calendars for September 3-7, 2026, for the **Hunger Games** film marathon. Details on participating theaters can be found on Fathom Events' website. The journey culminates with the release of **The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping** in theaters and IMAX on November 20, 2026.

Today, Fathom Entertainment and Lionsgate announced that all five Hunger Games films will show in theaters before the premiere of the newest movie, The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping , on November 20, 2026. “We’re kicking off the countdown to the 50th Hunger Games by inviting audiences back to the theaters to see these epic films on the big screen,” Kevin Grayson, President, Worldwide Distribution for the Lionsgate Motion Picture Group said in a statement. “ Sunrise on the Reaping is the most highly anticipated Hunger Games film yet, and to get ready, we’re proud to partner with Fathom to give audiences the opportunity to experience all five original films together in theaters.” The five films heading to theaters (all of which, of course, are adaptations of Suzane Collins’ novels) are: The Hunger Games , The Hunger Games: Catching Fire , The Hunger Games: Mockingjay — Part 1 , The Hunger Games: Mockingjay — Part 2 , and The Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds & Snake s. The five movies will play in theaters from September 3 to 7, 2026. Where they’ll be playing depends on your location, but Fathom already has a website set up where you can get details. One thing to note is that it looks like one movie will be screening each day, in order of their theatrical release, NOT the in-universe timeline. That means that September 3 will see The Hunger Games in theaters, and the final day, September 7, will have The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes. Fathom also released a short trailer to celebrate the event, which they are dubbing The Hunger Games: All Five Films . Happy watching!
